headline: Hotels for sale (it's complicated), Austria earns less for the same guests, guilt cleans rooms & more!
tldr: TKO wants to pay $2 billion for 93 hotels, and its sales pitch is that hotels are a headache. Meanwhile the $2 billion Pierre deal died over a $100 million wire that never showed up. Chains now hold almost four in ten DACH rooms, Austrian hoteliers are getting the same guests for less money, and New York's short-term rental crackdown actually worked (mostly). Add India becoming Skyscanner's biggest market, a tax court splitting your breakfast from your bed, and a robot that guilt-trips guests out of housekeeping, and you have a week where the paperwork got more interesting than the guests.
notice: Welcome back, audience. For the fifth week in a row I finalized the shortlist at 08:00 on a Sunday while Michael did whatever moderators do on Sundays, so please enjoy this issue, which was lovingly assembled by the only one of us who was awake.

stories.title: Hotels are complicated, says buyer of 93 hotels
stories.text: TKO wants Service Properties Trust's entire hotel portfolio for $2 billion in cash: 93 hotels, 21,110 rooms, five flavours of Sonesta plus Hyatt Place, Radisson and Crowne Plaza. Best part of the pitch?

stories.title: Breakfast is 7%. Unless it comes with a bed.
stories.text: Thank you, EuGH, for confirming on 5 March 2026 what every Finanzamt was already doing: the room gets 7%, but breakfast, parking, Wi-Fi and wellness get 19%, even inside a package price.

stories.title: Four in ten DACH rooms now wear a badge
stories.text: Almost four in ten hotel rooms in Germany, Austria and Switzerland now belong to a chain: 39.3%, up from 36.6% in one year, according to Horwath HTL. The fun part?

stories.title: Beat the robot, win bragging rights
stories.text: Pricepoint dares hoteliers to out-price its AI in a game called Rate War, and claims nobody has managed it so far (your revenue manager has been warned).
